item.description: Publicly listed Sun Insurance Company Ltd (SPX:SUN) has cleared the air on its engagement with former Fijian Holdings Ltd chief executive officer Nouzab Fareed, who was recently found guilty of two counts of indecent assault. “SUN had provided a consultancy assignment to Mohammed Nouzab Fareed, as chief transformational consultant, over a period of 20 months. This assignment has now successfully c
item.content:encoded:
Publicly listed Sun Insurance Company Ltd (SPX:SUN) has cleared the air on its engagement with former Fijian Holdings Ltd chief executive officer Nouzab Fareed, who was recently found guilty of two counts of indecent assault.

“SUN had provided a consultancy assignment to Mohammed Nouzab Fareed, as chief transformational consultant, over a period of 20 months. This assignment has now successfully completed and concluded,” the general insurer said in a statement filed at the South Pacific Stock Exchange (SPX) on Tuesday.

“SUN wishes to clarify that the company is aware of the recent publicity regarding its consultant.

“The company is aware that the matter relates to Mr Fareed’s previous employment and acknowledges the court’s decision. The matter does not relate to Sun Insurance Company Ltd’s operations, financial reporting or its customers.

“The board would like to acknowledge Mr Fareed for his sterling work in carrying out the objectives set for him within the confined period.”

Mr Fareed was appointed chief transformation officer for SUN last year.

item.title: Citizens budget to enhance transparency and understanding
item.description: Every Fijian regardless of their language or background will now be able to better understand the 2026-27 National Budget after the launch of the Citizens’ Guide to the National Budget in English, Hindi and iTaukei. During the launch at the Ministry of Finance office in Suva on Wednesday, Minister for Finance Esrom Immanuel said the Citizens’ Budget will enhance transparency and accountability.
item.content:encoded:
Every Fijian regardless of their language or background will now be able to better understand the 2026-27 National Budget after the launch of the Citizens’ Guide to the National Budget in English, Hindi and iTaukei.

During the launch at the Ministry of Finance office in Suva on Wednesday, Minister for Finance Esrom Immanuel said the Citizens’ Budget will enhance transparency and accountability.

He said publishing the Citizens’ Budget in three main languages will enable every citizen to understand the government’s priorities and appreciate how public resources are being invested to improve their lives.

“The Citizens’ Budget distils key information into a concise and reader-friendly 20-page publication,” Mr Immanuel said.

“It outlines the government’s revenue and expenditure plans, major policy priorities in infrastructure, health, education and social protection and the key economic forecast as well as the medium-term fiscal strategy,” he said.

Mr Immanuel said the 2026-27 national budget was formulated during a period of considerable economic uncertainty.

“The global fuel and energy crisis that placed significant pressure on the economy, public finances and the cost of living, requiring the government to make careful and responsible policy choices.

“At the same time, government had to make provision for several major national priorities that could not be deferred including funding for the general election, constitutional referendum, the national census and the commencement of major capital projects that are critical to Fiji’s long-term development and future prosperity,” he said.

“This reflects a disciplined and balanced fiscal approach, one that continues to invest in Fiji’s long-term development while safeguarding fiscal sustainability,” he said.

He said the government has looked at the welfare of the people and the economy to ensure the economy keeps functioning despite the crisis faced.

item.title: Optimism for higher growth
item.description: Government has defended the economic growth of 1.5 per cent as forecasted in the 2026-27 National Budget, saying it was prepared based on a worst-case scenario considering the geopolitical issues affecting the country. Following the ANZ’s Pacific Insight Report in which ANZ’s senior Pacific economist Dr Kishti Sen highlighted that the local economic growth would outpace the budgeted forecast, Mini
item.content:encoded:
Government has defended the economic growth of 1.5 per cent as forecasted in the 2026-27 National Budget, saying it was prepared based on a worst-case scenario considering the geopolitical issues affecting the country.

Following the ANZ’s Pacific Insight Report in which ANZ’s senior Pacific economist Dr Kishti Sen highlighted that the local economic growth would outpace the budgeted forecast, Minister for Finance Esrom Immanuel said the economic growth will be better than what had been forecasted in the budget.

“It will be better than what we budgeted, because we prepared this budget on a worst-case scenario, projecting that this fuel crisis and the effect of it or the ramification of it will go on for another six or nine months,” Mr Immanuel said.

“As you can see in the global news that the war is still happening. So, it will go on for some time. But we believe that we can do and we’ll do better based on ANZ’s projections,” he said.

Mr Immanuel said if the economic performance exceeds expectations and generates a surplus, then the additional funds would be used in key priority areas.

“Any surplus will probably be used in three areas—for future needs, reducing government debt, and supporting other important priorities, whether that is infrastructure development or other sectors that require assistance,” he said.

Meanwhile, in the ANZ Pacific Insight Report, Dr Sen has projected that Fiji’s 2026 economic growth will outpace the Government’s 1.5 per cent “worst-case” budget projection.

He said they are forecasting real gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 2.7 per cent this year and 2027, driven by record remittances, tourism and rising agricultural exports.

In a similar report released earlier this month, Dr Sen said the national budget had assumed a worst-case set of economic assumptions to project revenue.

item.title: PEOPLE | Camari refuses to quit: Dream gets clearer at car wash
item.description: Lately, the sound of running water blaring music, the scent of cleaning chemicals and the hum of passing traffic have become part of Camari Adiseuga Vere’s daily routine. At 29, she spends her days washing, scrubbing and polishing vehicles at her family’s car wash in Korovou, Tailevu.
item.content:encoded:
Lately, the sound of running water blaring music, the scent of cleaning chemicals and the hum of passing traffic have become part of Camari Adiseuga Vere’s daily routine.

At 29, she spends her days washing, scrubbing and polishing vehicles at her family’s car wash in Korovou, Tailevu.

It is honest work, and she does it with pride. But beneath the satisfaction she gives her customers, is a dream that refuses to go away.

Camari once dreamed of becoming an automotive engineer.

That dream was put on hold when she dropped out of school in Form Six because of personal problems at home.

For many, this would have marked the end of their ambitions.

For Camari, it simply meant taking a different road.

Today, she helps her father operate the family-owned car wash, serving loyal customers who return because of the quality of service they receive. Others stop in after noticing the business while driving through Korovou.

Prices range from $10 to $40, depending on the size of the vehicle. Every automobile is treated with the same care, whether it is a small car or a large truck

“There are busy days and there are slow days,” she said.

“But that doesn’t change how we serve our customers. We always give our best because we want them to come back and choose us again.”

Like many small business owners, the family has had to adjust to rising operating costs.

The recent increase in fuel prices has also affected the cost of running the business, but Camari said most customers understood the reasons behind the price adjustments.

The car wash enjoys a peaceful setting beside the river, surrounded by greenery, offering customers the perfect place to de-stress while their vehicles are cleaned. Although she spends her days washing cars, her interest has always been in understanding how they work.

As a young girl, she often watched her father repair vehicles. Those moments sparked a fascination with engines and mechanics that has stayed with her ever since. She still hopes to one day return to school and fulfil her childhood dream of becoming an automotive engineer.

“It would be nice to go back to school,” she said.

“But for now, my focus is helping with the car wash until dad is able to manage the business on his own.”

She also has plans to improve the business by building a comfortable seating area where customers can relax while waiting for their vehicles.

Her message to young people who have dropped out of school is:”Never look down on yourself. Never give up in life.

“Find a way to overcome your problems and keep working hard.

“You can become whatever you want to be.

“Believe in yourself, and one day you will get there.”

item.title: Witchcraft claim emerges in murder inquiry
item.description: A senior medical officer has told the High Court that Naqali murder accused Samuela Dasalusalu acknowledged having schizophrenia but believed his condition was caused by witchcraft rather than a medical illness. Dr Faurina Panapasa told Justice Pita Bulamainaivalu that Mr Dasalusalu has a longstanding history of chronic schizophrenia and had been admitted to St Giles Hospital 23 times, mainly due
item.content:encoded:
A senior medical officer has told the High Court that Naqali murder accused Samuela Dasalusalu acknowledged having schizophrenia but believed his condition was caused by witchcraft rather than a medical illness.

Dr Faurina Panapasa told Justice Pita Bulamainaivalu that Mr Dasalusalu has a longstanding history of chronic schizophrenia and had been admitted to St Giles Hospital 23 times, mainly due to stopping medication and substance abuse, which led to relapses involving hallucinations and threatening behaviour.

The court earlier this month granted the State’s application for an inquiry into Mr Dasalusalu’s mental state under Section 104 of the Criminal Procedure Act after three psychiatric evaluation reports concluded that Mr Dasalusalu remained unfit to stand trial or enter a plea.

Dr Panapasa, who prepared the first psychiatric report dated January 2, 2026, said Mr Dasalusalu reported hearing voices on the day of the alleged offence, telling him “the person bullying you is coming”. He claimed he armed himself with a cane knife, chased 16-year-old Salote Sikiti and struck her after she fell.

The High Court is conducting an inquiry into Dasalusalu’s mental state after three psychiatric reports found he remains unfit to stand trial or enter a plea.

item.title: Bail denied for former CEO
item.description: Former Fiji Holdings Ltd (FHL) chief executive officer Mohammed Nouzab Fareed will remain in custody after the Chief Magistrate dismissed his application for release pending sentencing. Chief Magistrate Josaia Waqaivolavola ruled that Fareed’s conviction meant he had lost his right to freedom of movement.
item.content:encoded:
Former Fiji Holdings Ltd (FHL) chief executive officer Mohammed Nouzab Fareed will remain in custody after the Chief Magistrate dismissed his application for release pending sentencing.

Chief Magistrate Josaia Waqaivolavola ruled that Fareed’s conviction meant he had lost his right to freedom of movement.

Fareed was convicted of two counts of indecent assault involving a young female subordinate. The court found he hugged, sniffed, and kissed the complainant without her consent during the first incident, and during the second incident in his office, sniffed her hair, kissed her forehead, touched her ear, and placed his hands around her chest without consent.

The complainant’s evidence was supported by an audio recording accepted by the court.

Sentencing, initially set for August 12, has been brought forward to August 7.

item.title: Judge seeks COI clarity
item.description: The High Court in Suva has directed the parties in the judicial review challenging the Commission of Inquiry (COI) into the appointment of FICAC Commissioner Barbara Malimali to provide clarifications ahead of a judgment set for August 3. In a Minute issued on July 28, 2026, Justice Dane Tuiqereqere ordered the matter to be called for mention this morning at 9am.
item.content:encoded:
The High Court in Suva has directed the parties in the judicial review challenging the Commission of Inquiry (COI) into the appointment of FICAC Commissioner Barbara Malimali to provide clarifications ahead of a judgment set for August 3.

In a Minute issued on July 28, 2026, Justice Dane Tuiqereqere ordered the matter to be called for mention this morning at 9am.

The direction follows a three-day substantive hearing which took place in April.

Justice Tuiqereqere has directed Government respondents, which include the COI, the President, the Prime Minister, and the Attorney-General, to confirm whether Ms Malimali and her legal representative were excluded from the courtroom during the oral evidence of key high-profile witnesses.

The list of witnesses cited in the Minute includes Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka (January 6, 2025), Chief Justice Salesi Temo (January 23 and February 27, 2025), Deputy Prime Minister Professor Biman Prasad (February 11, 2025), Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica (February 18, 2025) and other political figures and state officials.

If the respondents do not dispute the exclusion, the court requires them to provide the reasons given by the Commissioner for barring Ms Malimali and her lawyer, along with any relevant written minutes or transcripts.

The court has also instructed the respondents to produce a copy of a letter dated December 13, 2024, sent by Ms Mason to the Chief Justice, in which the Commission sought the suspension of Ms Malimali while its inquiry was under way.

The applicants are Ms Malimali, senior lawyers William Wylie Clarke, Laurel Vaurasi and former Attorney-General Graham Everett Leung. Justice David Ashton-Lewis, the Commissioner, is a third party in the proceedings.

item.title: Lawyer seeks time in appeal
item.description: A Supreme Court appeal involving Veronica Malani has been adjourned to October 14 after her newly appointed lawyer sought time to familiarise himself with the case. The appeal was called before Chief Justice Salesi Temo yesterday, when lawyer Sevuloni Valenitabua confirmed he had recently taken over the case. He informed the court that he had only received the case documents the previous day and r
item.content:encoded:
A Supreme Court appeal involving Veronica Malani has been adjourned to October 14 after her newly appointed lawyer sought time to familiarise himself with the case.

The appeal was called before Chief Justice Salesi Temo yesterday, when lawyer Sevuloni Valenitabua confirmed he had recently taken over the case. He informed the court that he had only received the case documents the previous day and requested time to review them.

The case stems from Ms Malani’s attempt to challenge a decision by the Director of Public Prosecutions not to charge former attorney-general Aiyaz Sayed-Khaiyum over allegations relating to two bombing incidents in 1987.

Ms Malani lodged a complaint with police in July 2020, alleging Mr Sayed-Khaiyum’s involvement in the incidents and seeking possible charges, including murder, assault causing grievous bodily harm and attempting to injure by explosive substance. Following investigations, police referred the file to the Office of the DPP, which announced in January 2021 that no charges would be laid.

The High Court dismissed her subsequent application for leave to seek judicial review of the DPP’s decision in September 2021. A later application for leave to appeal was also unsuccessful.

In June 2025, the Court of Appeal refused Ms Malani leave to appeal against the High Court’s decision, ruling the appeal had no realistic prospect of success nor did it raise any matters of public interest or importance or relate to any novel legal issues.

Ms Malani then appealed to the Supreme Court.
